reasoning_traces.think:
The MIND corpus is fundamentally composed of conceptual claims rather than numerical game quantities. Only 5.2% of premises are probability-gradeable, leaving 94.8% context-scoped without probabilistic framing. To grade these, we must shift from binary game outcome comparisons to real-game quantity measurement. The core insight is that a premise’s validity should be assessed by comparing its claimed direction against empirical game behavior—such as whether higher separation predicts greater receiving yards. This requires verifying that the relevant measure surfaces exist in the database (14/87 contexts currently measurable), and that the premise type supports such validation (correlational/causal). Failure occurs when numeric values are placeholders or when no game-relevant quantity is specified. The universal lens unifies this into a single operator: contextual concept grading, where directionality is validated against real-world outcomes.
